data.title: UK retail sales increase 2.3% Y/Y in October, topping estimates
data.description:
• The UK’s retail sales volumes increased 0.7% M/M in October 2026, beating economists’ expectations for no growth, according to data released by the Office for National Statistics. The increase followed a 0.4% decline in September.
  • On a Y/Y basis, retail sales volumes rose 2.3%, accelerating from 0.8% growth in the previous month and exceeding consensus estimates of 1.7%.
  • The stronger-than-expected reading points to an improvement in consumer spending, with both monthly and annual retail sales growth exceeding market forecasts.

data.description: Singapore's consumer-price index likely rose 1.9% on year in October, slowing from September's 2.2% increase, according to the median estimate of six economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. Core CPI, which excludes private road transport and accommodation prices, likely rose 1.6% in October, easing from September's 2.0% rise, according to the poll. The softer CPI prints expected will reflect the impact of lower electricity tariffs in 4Q, as well as high base effects, UOB economist Jester Koh says in a note. data.title: U.S. Treasury Yields Fall as Investors Seek Safe-Haven Assets
data.description:
By Miriam Mukuru

U.S. Treasury yields dropped in Asian trade on Friday as risk-off sentiment continued to drive demand for safe-haven assets.

The two-year Treasury yield fell 5.5 basis points to 4.724%, while the 10-year yield dropped 4.4 bps to 5.008%, according to Tradeweb. Twenty-year Treasury yields declined 3.2 bps to 5.419%.

A record initial public offering by Anthropic, which raised $81 billion, failed to revive appetite for artificial-intelligence stocks. Investors continued to question whether the enormous investments in the AI industry would pay off given the rising public resistance toward the industry.

"The blockbuster debut [IPO] couldn't sweep those worries under the rug," Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote, said in a note.

High borrowing costs also raise concerns about the AI companies' ability to continue raising funds to finance their massive expansion.

"The scale of the Democratic win in the midterm [elections] has deepened worry that policymakers could push for slower data-center spending," David Groman, global equity strategist at Citi, said in a note.

The concerns about the tech and AI sector are driving the flight to safety, causing government bond yields to drop, Groman said.

IntelliAM AI PLC Wins National AI Innovation Award

Recognition at the Made in the UK Awards 2026 highlights the Company's innovation in industrial artificial intelligence

IntelliAM AI PLC, a technology company specialising in industrial artificial intelligence, machine learning and asset intelligence solutions for the manufacturing sector, is pleased to announce that it has been named AI Tech Innovation of the Year at the Made in the UK Awards 2026, organised by Insider Media.

The award, presented at a ceremony in Manchester on 19 November 2026, recognises the Company's innovation and contribution to the application of artificial intelligence within UK manufacturing.

The national recognition follows IntelliAM's earlier success at the Made in Yorkshire Awards 2026.

Supporting Innovation in Manufacturing

IntelliAM combines industrial engineering expertise with artificial intelligence, machine learning and advanced data analytics to help manufacturers improve equipment reliability, optimise maintenance strategies and reduce unplanned downtime.

The Company's technology is designed to enable manufacturers to make better use of their existing operational data, identifying developing equipment issues and supporting more informed operational decisions.

The award recognises IntelliAM's approach to developing practical industrial AI solutions and the contribution of its engineering, software development and product teams, working alongside customers and partners.

Tom Clayton, Chief Executive Officer of IntelliAM AI PLC, commented:

"We are delighted to receive this national recognition, which is a significant achievement for IntelliAM and reflects the dedication and expertise of our teams.

"Our focus has always been on developing AI technology that addresses real challenges within manufacturing, helping businesses improve reliability, efficiency and operational performance.

"Following our success at the Made in Yorkshire Awards, this national award provides further recognition of our approach to industrial AI and the work we are doing to make advanced technology more accessible and valuable to manufacturers.

"We look forward to building on this achievement as we continue to develop our technology and strengthen our relationships with customers and partners."

The Edinburgh Investment Trust Plc

HALF-YEARLY FINANCIAL REPORT

FOR THE SIX MONTHS TO 30 SEPTEMBER 2026

20 November 2026 - The Directors of the Edinburgh Investment Trust plc ("the Company") have today announced the half year results for the six-month period ended 30 September 2026.

Highlights

  • Net asset value (“NAV”) total return of 8.0% over the period
  • The share price at the period end was 830p, a total return of 9.7% over the period
  • The share price discount to NAV narrowed to 7.4% (from 8.6% as at 31 March 2026)
  • A first interim dividend of 8.4p per share has been declared, 10.5% higher than the first interim dividend last year and comfortably ahead of UK CPI inflation of 3.5%
  • Since March 2020, when Liontrust began managing the Company’s portfolio, the annualised NAV and share price total returns were 14.1% and 15.4% respectively, ahead of the FTSE All-Share Index annualised total return of 13.7%

Elisabeth Stheeman, Chair, said: “Since the Company’s year-end at 31 March 2026, the NAV total return was 8.0% and the share price returned 9.7%, both ahead of the total return of 7.2% from the benchmark FTSE All-Share Index. The stronger share price return was principally because the discount narrowed from 8.6% to 7.4%. It is pleasing to see that performance relative to the benchmark index has improved in the last six months.

We continue to work hard to raise the profile of the Company. The Manager continues to engage with a range of shareholders and potential shareholders. As a Board, we recently hosted a well-attended Annual General Meeting in Edinburgh and a presentation to retail investors in London. Other shareholder engagement activities included our stand at the Association of Investment Companies (AIC) showcase event and Deputy Portfolio Manager Emily Barnard speaking on a panel at the ‘Investor Summit’ event for private investors in September. As a Board we are delighted that there is such excellent engagement across the Company’s shareholder base.

The portfolio’s diversification, the quality of its holdings and their valuations leave the Company well placed to deliver attractive long-term total returns for shareholders.”

Imran Sattar, Portfolio Manager, said: “In the six months under review, the UK market enjoyed a further period of solid performance. There was notable continued strength in the Banks sector, with the current interest rate environment driving higher profit expectations. There was also a pick-up in Energy and Basic Materials. Positive contributions came from stocks with a variety of different economic characteristics. Softcat, the IT infrastructure technology provider, issued a strong trading update and upgraded its full-year guidance. NatWest also performed well. Rotork shares responded positively to a bid from ABB at a 73% premium, while Anglo American continued to benefit from high copper prices and progress towards completing its merger with Teck Resources.

During the period, we took new holdings in Weir, SigmaRoc, IntegraFin, Bellway, Persimmon, British American Tobacco and Aviva. These investments provide exposure to a range of different growth drivers, including increased mining expenditure, European reindustrialisation, growth in investment platforms and the UK housing market.

The global economic outlook remains mixed and challenging. Trade tensions and geopolitical risks continue to create uncertainty. The range of potential outcomes across geopolitics, technology and financial markets remains unusually wide, which has led us to introduce greater stylistic balance to the portfolio. The management of the portfolio remains highly active and differentiated from the index, with exposure to multiple distinct themes. This balance should leave the portfolio better positioned to participate across a broader range of market conditions.”

About The Edinburgh Investment Trust

The Edinburgh Investment Trust was established in March 1889 and has been managed by the current team since March 2020, with Imran Sattar taking over as Portfolio Manager in October 2023, and Emily Barnard as Deputy Portfolio Manager in February 2024.

The portfolio management team construct a high-conviction portfolio of 40 to 50 holdings based on fundamental company research. Up to 20% of the portfolio may be invested in non-UK stocks.

The team’s flexible investment process delivers a differentiated, diversified portfolio of listed equities.

Investment objective

The Company aims to exceed the total return on the FTSE All-Share Index and grow its dividend faster than UK inflation (CPI). This objective will be assessed over the long term and performance against the FTSE All-Share Index will be measured on a NAV total return basis.

Investment policy

The Company invests primarily in the shares of companies quoted on a recognised stock exchange in the UK. Securities of companies quoted on a recognised stock exchange outside of the UK may also be held but will not exceed 20% of the market value of the investment portfolio, measured at the time of any acquisition.

The portfolio is selected by the Portfolio Manager, and monitored carefully by the Board, on the basis of the Portfolio Manager’s assessment of the fundamental value available in individual securities, whilst giving due regard to sector and industry weightings and to broader economic and market conditions. Companies are chosen by the Portfolio Manager on the basis of their individual business strengths, growth and income characteristics and valuation, and not according to specific rules of asset allocation.

Borrowings may be used to provide gearing to the equity portfolio of up to 25% of net assets.

Investment decisions are restricted by the following:

  • No acquisition may be made which would result in a holding being greater than 10% of the market value of the investment portfolio;
  • The Company will not invest more than 15% of its total assets in the shares of other UK-listed investment trusts or investment companies;
  • The Company will not hold more than 5% of the issued share capital (or voting shares) of any one company.

In addition, the Company may:

  • invest in convertibles (securities which are typically expected to convert into shares on a recognised stock exchange) subject to no acquisition or conversion resulting in a holding breaching the limits in this investment policy;
  • use derivative instruments, monitored carefully by the Board and subject to constraints, including the writing of covered calls against securities (which in aggregate amount to no more than 10% of the value of the investment portfolio) and the investment in FTSE 100 futures (subject to the value of such positions, if exercised, not exceeding 15% of the value of the investment portfolio). Other derivative instruments may be employed, subject to prior Board approval, provided that the cost (and potential liability) of exercise of all outstanding derivative positions should not exceed 25% of the value of the investment portfolio at any time;
  • hedge exposure to changes in foreign currency rates in respect of its overseas investments.

Nature of the company

The Company is registered in Scotland with number SC001836 and is registered as an investment company under Section 833 of the Companies Act 2006.

The principal activity of the Company is that of an investment trust company within the meaning of section 1158 of the Corporation Tax Act 2010.

The Company is a FTSE 250 Investment Company whose shares are listed on the London Stock Exchange (‘LSE’). The business of the Company consists of investing its assets according to a specified investment objective and policy, with the aim of diversifying investment risk and generating a return for shareholders.

The Company uses borrowing to enhance returns to shareholders. This increases the risk to shareholders should the value of investments fall.

The Company has contracted with an external manager, Liontrust Fund Partners LLP (‘LFP’ or ‘the Manager’) to act as its Alternative Investment Fund Manager (‘AIFM’) and to manage its investments. Other administrative functions are contracted to external service providers. The Company has a Board of non-executive directors who oversee and monitor the activities of the Manager and other service providers on behalf of shareholders and ensure that the investment objective and policy are adhered to. The Company has no employees.

The Company’s ordinary shares qualify as mainstream investment products suitable for promotion to both retail and professional investors. The Company’s ordinary shares are eligible for investment in an ISA.

Chair’s Statement

At the end of September, the Company’s share price was 830p (30 September 2025: 800p) and the Net Asset Value (“NAV”) per share was 896p (30 September 2025: 866p). Since the Company’s year-end at 31 March 2026, the NAV total return was 8.0% and the share price returned 9.7%, both ahead of the total return of 7.2% from the benchmark FTSE All-Share Index. The share price return was higher than the NAV return principally because the discount narrowed from 8.6% to 7.4% in this period. We declared a first interim dividend of 8.4p per share last month, up 10.5% from the equivalent point last year and comfortably exceeding UK inflation of 3.5%.

We are conscious that the Company’s longer-term returns, including over three and five years, have lagged the index. As a Board, we recognise the importance of getting investment performance back on track. As I outlined in the annual report and at the Annual General Meeting and Retail Shareholder event, we have engaged closely with the Manager and it is pleasing to see that performance relative to the benchmark index has improved in the last six months and we hope this will be sustained.

Another relevant period for assessing longer-term performance is the period since March 2020, when Liontrust’s Global Fundamental team began managing the Company. Over these six and a half years, the annualised NAV and share price total returns were 14.1% and 15.4% respectively, outperforming the FTSE All-Share Index annualised total return of 13.7%.

DIVIDEND

As noted above, a first interim dividend of 8.4p per share was declared in October. In the absence of any material change in market conditions and/or income levels, we would also expect to announce a second interim dividend of 8.4p in January. In accounting terms, the Company’s first-half revenue return per share was 13.9p, slightly down from 14.0p last year. This means that the expected dividends for the first half are modestly uncovered, at an expected 16.8p versus a revenue return of 13.9p. The 2.9p shortfall is being funded from the Company’s accumulated revenue reserves, which is consistent with the approach taken in recent years.

I would like to remind shareholders of a small change to the timing of the Company’s dividend payments, which was approved at last July’s Annual General Meeting. We will now pay a fourth interim dividend three months after the third interim dividend. This means that shareholders will receive all four dividends at three-month intervals. The timetable of payments is on the Company’s website: www.edinburgh-investment-trust.co.uk.

BORROWINGS

We announced in October that a new £25 million multicurrency Revolving Credit Facility had been agreed with the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) Limited, London Branch. The Facility matures in October 2027 and can be extended annually. It provides an additional flexible source of gearing alongside the Company’s unsecured senior loan notes, which have an aggregate par value of £120m and a weighted average maturity of 21 years. At 30 September 2026 the portfolio’s net gearing (with debt at par) was 10.1% and net gearing (with debt at fair value) was 4.3%. This Facility, if fully drawn, would represent an additional 2.4% of gearing at par and 2.3% at fair value. Together, these borrowing arrangements provide the Company with a flexible and long-term source of gearing. The existing loan notes have contributed positively to NAV returns since they were issued in 2022.

SHARE PRICE DISCOUNT TO NET ASSET VALUE

In common with many other investment trusts, the Company’s shares trade at a discount to net asset value. This has narrowed over the period from 8.6% to 7.4% and, at the time of writing, is 7.4%. In addition to the absolute level of the discount, we also monitor the discount relative to peers, as well as against the Company’s own history. Over the period we bought back 6.9% of the Company’s shares. If the recent improvement in performance is sustained and reflected in a narrower discount, we would expect the need for buybacks to reduce.

SHAREHOLDER ENGAGEMENT

We continue to work hard to raise the profile of the Company and generate additional demand for the Company’s shares. For example, the Manager continues to engage with a range of shareholders and potential shareholders across the wealth manager and institutional parts of the market. As a Board, we have recently hosted two important shareholder events: a well-attended Annual General Meeting in Edinburgh in July and a lively presentation to retail investors in central London in October. Thank you to all the shareholders who attended one or both events. Highlights of these presentations have since been posted to the Company’s website. We will flag other events and presentations on the website and via other media, including social media channels as we reach out to a wider audience. I also encourage shareholders to subscribe to Company updates through the website and follow the Company on LinkedIn.

The Company is well placed to deliver attractive total returns to shareholders.

Other shareholder engagement activities are also underway. For example, shareholders may have seen our stand at the Association of Investment Companies (AIC) showcase event in London in October – another event with excellent attendance – or heard Deputy Portfolio Manager Emily Barnard speaking on a panel at the ‘Investor Summit’ event for private investors in London in September. As a Board we are delighted that there is such excellent engagement across the Company’s shareholder base.

BOARD SUCCESSION

On 1 September we appointed Claire Boyle as a Director. Claire brings a wealth of experience from the financial sector and chairs Fidelity Special Values investment trust and is the audit committee chair of the Monks investment trust. We are delighted that Claire has joined the Board.

OUTLOOK

The Company is well placed to deliver attractive total returns to shareholders. This will be driven by the Portfolio Managers’ investment process, with the portfolio fully invested across a range of high-quality businesses, typically with attractive long-term growth prospects. In addition, the Company’s borrowings provide the potential to enhance long‑term returns.

Set against this, high and growing levels of government debt around the world are a concern. This has led to some weakness in the major government bond markets, but so far, it has had a limited impact on equity markets. Portfolio Managers’ Report

For The Period Ended 30 September 2026

As a brief reminder of our approach to managing the Company’s assets, we aim to deliver an attractive long-term total return through a combination of income and capital growth.

To do this, we apply an investment process to identify and invest in a portfolio of businesses that, in aggregate, offer these income and growth characteristics. The process is flexible, with an open-minded approach to investment style, for example across growth, value, and recovery stocks. At the period end, the portfolio consisted of 42 stocks and was well diversified both economically and thematically.

PERFORMANCE REVIEW

In the six months under review, the UK market enjoyed a further period of solid performance. There was notable continued strength in the Banks sector, with the current interest rate environment driving higher profit expectations. There was also a pickup in Energy and Basic Materials in the latter part of the period, supported by continued geopolitical uncertainty.

Over the period, the NAV total return was 8.0% and the share price total return was 9.7%, both ahead of the 7.2% return from the benchmark FTSE All-Share index.

Positive contributions came from stocks with a variety of different economic characteristics. Softcat, the IT infrastructure technology provider, issued a strong trading update and upgraded its full-year guidance. NatWest also performed well, benefiting from the supportive interest rate environment referred to above. Rotork shares responded positively to a bid from ABB at a 73% premium, while Anglo American continued to benefit from high copper prices and progress towards completing its merger with Teck Resources.

The most significant detractors from relative performance were Rolls-Royce and Rentokil. Rolls-Royce was not held in the portfolio during the period and was therefore a relative detractor as its shares continued to perform strongly. We have kept the company under close review and, following the period end, used a period of share price weakness to initiate a position. Rentokil is one of the larger positions in the portfolio. The shares underperformed significantly after the new CEO removed the North American margin target and the company reported slightly weaker top-line growth. The current share price fairly balances Rentokil’s potential risks and rewards, including the new management team successfully reinvigorating the business and the opportunity for margin expansion and profit growth. The position remains under careful review.

PORTFOLIO ACTIVITY AND DIVERSIFICATION

During the period, we took new holdings in Weir, SigmaRoc, IntegraFin, Bellway, Persimmon, British American Tobacco (‘BATS’) and Aviva. These investments provide exposure to a range of different growth drivers, including increased mining expenditure, European reindustrialisation, growth in investment platforms and the UK housing market.

Weir is a high-quality mining equipment business, with most of its revenue generated from the sale of replacement parts for heavy machinery. This recurring revenue base gives the business greater resilience than more cyclical mining capital equipment companies. Share price weakness early in the period, reflecting market concerns around order momentum, first-half/second-half phasing and Weir’s competitive position, created an attractive entry point. We believe the competitive concerns are overstated, given Weir’s strong position in mission-critical slurry pumps, and that the business has an attractive medium-term outlook.

SigmaRoc is a European lime and essential minerals producer with leading positions across its core markets. Lime is an attractive niche market. It is essential across a wide range of industrial, environmental and construction end-markets, is difficult to substitute and typically represents a small share of customers’ overall costs. We believe the business is well positioned to benefit from volume recovery, pricing, infrastructure and defence spending, and further bolt-on M&A. The valuation does not appear to reflect the potential for margin expansion and earnings accretion from these drivers.

IntegraFin owns Transact, a high-quality investment platform for financial advisers that continues to gain share in a fragmented market. The business should be able to sustain attractive organic net flows, supported by its strong service proposition and long-standing adviser relationships. Following a period of increased investment, cost growth should normalise, supporting margin expansion.

Our investments in housebuilders Persimmon and Bellway offer somewhat different exposures. We believe both are well placed to generate strong profit growth and free cash flow, even without a significant recovery in housing volumes. Both investments were made before the announcement of support for first-time buyers, reflecting our view that the companies can grow from current levels without relying on government stimulus.

Persimmon should benefit from continued outlet growth and its well-positioned product offering. Among the national housebuilders, it has the lowest average selling price and greatest exposure to northern England and first-time buyers, which should leave it well placed to benefit from any government measures to support the housing market. Bellway, meanwhile, should benefit from internal improvements to cash generation, which should support further share buybacks and dividends. Both companies have strong balance sheets, which should provide resilience while industry volumes remain weak.

BATS is a global tobacco and nicotine products company. Its core ‘combustibles’ business is highly cash generative and should continue to fund attractive dividends and share buybacks. The company’s next-generation products are growing faster than the rest of the group, and we believe its brands have strong market positions and attractive growth prospects. We view the current valuation as an attractive entry point, given the company’s cash generation, growth prospects and potential shareholder returns.

Aviva is a leading provider of insurance, wealth management, and retirement services. Under the current CEO, the business has been simplified and is now more focused on its core UK, Ireland, and Canada operations, while also becoming more capital-light. The company has strong market positions across its divisions and continues to focus on growing higher-return earnings streams. We believe Aviva offers an attractive combination of earnings growth and shareholder returns at the current valuation.

Material sales during the period can be grouped into the following categories:

  • Consolidating exposure within the Data and Analytics theme into our highest-conviction holdings. This resulted in the complete sale of our positions in MONY Group and Trainline.
  • Changes to consumer-exposed positions. We sold our positions in Greggs and Whitbread as our conviction in their investment cases had declined. This created capacity to invest in Bellway and Persimmon without increasing the portfolio’s overall exposure to the UK consumer.
  • Valuation discipline. We exited positions in Renishaw, Oxford Instruments and Diploma – all had performed strongly, both operationally and in share price terms. However, they had reached valuation levels that we considered fully reflected their prospects.

BENCHMARK (OR BENCHMARK INDEX)

A standard against which performance can be measured, usually an index that averages the performance of companies in a stock market or a segment of the market. The Company’s benchmark is the FTSE All-Share Index.

Leverage, for the purposes of the UK AIFM Directive, is not synonymous with gearing as defined above. In addition to borrowings, it encompasses anything that increases the Company’s exposure, including foreign currency and exposure gained through derivatives. Leverage expresses the Company’s exposure as a ratio of the Company’s net asset value.

Accordingly, if a Company’s exposure was equal to its net assets it would have leverage of 100%. Two methods of calculating such exposure are set out in the AIFMD, gross and commitment. Under the gross method, exposure represents the aggregate of all the Company’s exposures other than cash balances held in base currency and without any offsetting. The commitment method takes into account hedging and other netting arrangements designed to limit risk, offsetting them against the underlying exposure.

RNS Number : 9729D Atlantic Lithium Limited 20 November 2026  

20 November 2026

AGM Statement

Atlantic Lithium Limited (AIM: ALL, ASX: A11, GSE: ALLGH, “Atlantic Lithium” or the “Company”), the Africa-focused lithium exploration and development company targeting the delivery of Ghana's first lithium mine, announces that at the Company’s Annual General Meeting (“AGM”), which will be held at 11:00 am (Perth time) today at the offices of HopgoodGanim Lawyers, Level 27, Allendale Square, 77 St Georges Terrace, Perth WA 6000, the Chairman of the AGM will issue the following statement:

“On behalf of the Board of Atlantic Lithium, I am pleased to welcome shareholders to the Company's 2026 Annual General Meeting.

“The past year has been a significant period for Atlantic Lithium, marked by progress towards the development of our flagship Ewoyaa Lithium Project in Ghana (“Ewoyaa” or “Project”) and the proposed acquisition of the Company by Huayou (Hong Kong) Company Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt Company Limited.

“A major achievement during the year was the ratification of the Mining Lease in respect of the Project by Ghana's Parliament in March 2026. The milestone highlights the Company's journey from the initial discovery of lithium at Ewoyaa, through exploration programmes, technical studies and permitting activities, to delivering the first Mining Lease to be granted, and subsequently ratified, for lithium in Ghana.

“Ratification followed extensive engagement with the Government of Ghana and other key stakeholders, providing greater regulatory certainty for the Project's future development. The achievement reaffirmed Ewoyaa’s strategic importance to Ghana and its potential to deliver significant long-term economic and social benefits to Ghanaians, particularly to the Project’s host communities.

“I would like to acknowledge the considerable efforts of our team and the support of the relevant government authorities and our local stakeholders in achieving this important outcome.

“As announced on 7 May 2026, Atlantic Lithium entered into a binding Scheme Implementation Deed with Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt Company Limited (“Huayou”), under which it is proposed that its subsidiary, Huayou (Hong Kong) Company Limited (“Huayou Sub”), will acquire 100% of the Company's issued share capital by way of an Australian scheme of arrangement (“Scheme”).

“The Atlantic Lithium Board unanimously recommends that shareholders vote in favour of the Scheme, in the absence of a superior proposal and subject to an independent expert continuing to conclude that the Scheme is in the best interests of Atlantic Lithium shareholders. Accordingly, the Atlantic Lithium Directors intend to vote, or cause to be voted, all Atlantic Lithium shares in which they have a relevant interest in, in favour of the Scheme.

“A copy of the Scheme Booklet is available on the Company’s website and on Atlantic Lithium’s ASX, AIM and GSE market announcement platforms.

“The Board recommends that shareholders read the Scheme Booklet and the Independent Expert’s Report in its entirety, including each of the reasons to vote for and against the Scheme, before deciding to vote on the Scheme (refer to section 1 of the Scheme Booklet). If shareholders are in doubt as to what they should do, they should consult their legal, financial taxation or other adviser. In considering the unanimous recommendation of the Atlantic Lithium Board to vote in favour of the Scheme, shareholders should have regard to the interests of the Atlantic Lithium Directors in the outcome of the Scheme and to certain payments to be made to a number of Atlantic Lithium Directors as set out in the Scheme Booklet (refer to footnote 6 of the Letter from the Chairman of Atlantic Lithium).

“The Scheme remains subject to the satisfaction or waiver of a number of conditions precedent, including regulatory approvals, approval by the requisite majority of Atlantic Lithium shareholders at the Scheme Meeting and approval by the Supreme Court of Western Australia. Further detail in relation to the conditions precedent are set out in section 3.7 of the Scheme Booklet which was released by the Company on 6 November 2026.

“An important milestone for Atlantic Lithium was the recent completion of the Novation Agreement, pursuant to which Piedmont Lithium Ghana Holdings, LLC, a subsidiary of Elevra Lithium Limited, sold all of its rights and interests in respect of the agreements related to Ewoyaa and the Company's broader lithium portfolio in Ghana to Huayou Sub.

“This formally established Huayou Sub as our new joint venture partner, bringing extensive technical expertise, financial resources and experience across the global supply chain to support Ewoyaa's advancement. Huayou's commitment to the Project serves as a strong endorsement of the work undertaken by Atlantic Lithium to date and reinforces our confidence in Ewoyaa's considerable potential.

“While separate from the proposed acquisition of Atlantic Lithium, the completion of the Novation Agreement represents a significant step in establishing a clear pathway for the Project's future development.

“The past year has again highlighted the volatility of the global lithium market, with recent price declines following periods of recovery. While the long-term fundamentals underpinning lithium demand remain encouraging, short-term price fluctuations continue to present challenges for emerging producers.

“These market conditions reinforce the importance of financial certainty and capital discipline; considerations which informed the Board's assessment of the proposed acquisition by Huayou and the opportunity it presents for shareholders to realise value. Again, the Board recommends that shareholders read the Scheme Booklet and the Independent Expert’s Report in its entirety, including each of the reasons to vote for and against the Scheme, before deciding to vote on the Scheme.

“As we look ahead, the Board remains confident in the strategic direction of the Project. We look forward to continuing our work with Huayou towards the development of the Project.

“On behalf of the Board, I extend my sincere thanks to our employees across Ghana and Australia for their unwavering commitment and professionalism. I would also like to thank our loyal shareholders for their ongoing support of the Company.”

data.title: REG - On the Beach Group - Board Change
data.description:
RNS Number : 9606D On the Beach Group PLC 20 November 2026  

20 November 2026

On the Beach Group plc

("On the Beach", "OTB" or the "Group")

Board Change

On the Beach Group plc (LSE: OTB.L) announces that Simon Cooper, the Group’s Founder, has informed the Board that he will step down from his non-executive Founder Director role and leave the Board on 1 December 2026, on the release of the Group’s full-year results.

Simon founded On the Beach in 2004 and was Chief Executive Officer until 2023, when he moved into his current non-executive role.

The Board has asked Elaine O’Donnell, Senior Independent Director and Chair of the Audit Committee, to continue to serve beyond the ninth anniversary of her appointment in July 2027, and Elaine has agreed. Elaine will stand for re-election at the Company’s 2027 Annual General Meeting and will step down from the Board on or before the conclusion of the 2028 Annual General Meeting. This will provide continuity on the Board and support an orderly handover to a new Audit Committee Chair ahead of the Group’s next external audit tender, due in 2028.

This announcement is made pursuant to UKLR 6.4.6R.

Simon Cooper, Founder of On the Beach, commented:

“It has been a privilege to build On the Beach, from a terraced house in Macclesfield in 2004 to the business it is today. That is down to the brilliant colleagues who have been part of the journey. The business is in great hands with Shaun and the team, with a clear strategy and exciting opportunities ahead, so this feels like the right time for me to step back. I remain a significant shareholder and continue to strongly support the Board and the Group’s strategy.”

Richard Pennycook, Chairman of On the Beach, said:

“Simon founded On the Beach in 2004 and, as Chief Executive for almost two decades, grew it from a start-up into one of the UK’s leading online package holiday companies. His entrepreneurial vision, deep sector knowledge and commitment have been instrumental in building the Group we are today. Few founders can pass the baton to an internal successor as effectively as Simon did with Shaun, and even fewer then remain on the Board to provide wise counsel while giving the new Chief Executive the space to lead. We are immensely grateful to Simon for his very significant contribution and wish him every success for the future.

“I am also delighted that Elaine has agreed to remain on the Board beyond nine years’ service. Elaine has been an excellent Senior Independent Director and Audit Committee Chair, and her rigour, judgement and deep knowledge of the business are hugely valued by the Board. Her continued contribution will ensure a smooth handover to her successor as we plan for the Board’s future composition.”

For further information:

On the Beach Group plc via Sodali

Shaun Morton, Chief Executive Officer

Jon Wormald, Chief Financial Officer

Sodali & Co       onthebeach@client.sodali.com

Rob Greening

Lizzy Kittle

About On the Beach

On the Beach Group plc is one of the UK's largest online package holiday specialists. We offer choice, value, flexibility and financial protection, powered by our proprietary technology platform.

With an asset-light, cash-generative model, we drive customer acquisition and loyalty through scalable technology, automation and operational efficiency, enabling us to grow profitably while helping more people holiday better and more often.

Renowned for beach package holidays, we have leveraged our expertise, technology and strong supplier relationships to broaden our addressable market, expanding into city breaks and cruise holidays, and offering our full range of holidays to customers in the Republic of Ireland.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Regulatory approvals and update on proposed acquisition of Community Unity Bank

London, 20 December, 07:00:

Further to the announcement of 17 March 2025 (RNS number 9000A) (the “Initial Announcement”), OakNorth Bank plc (the “Bank” or “OakNorth”) is pleased to announce that the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the “Federal Reserve”) and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency have given the requisite approval for completion of the proposed acquisition of Community Unity Bank (“CUB”).

Group restructuring

To meet the Federal Reserve’s requirements, the OakNorth group will undergo a restructuring of group entities. On completion, CUB will become a member of the group. The restructuring has also been approved by the Prudential Regulation Authority.

Timing and remaining steps

OakNorth anticipates completion of the transaction, including the restructuring of OakNorth’s group structure, by the end of 2026.

Effect on the Bank’s listed securities

The restructuring and the acquisition have no effect on the Bank’s listed securities. The Bank remains the issuer of its £150,000,000 10.000% Fixed Rate Reset Callable Subordinated Notes due 2035 (ISIN: XS2910525927) (the “Notes”), which are admitted to trading on the International Securities Market of the London Stock Exchange. There is no change to the terms of the Notes and no impact on the regulatory capital treatment of the Notes.

About OakNorth Bank plc

Launched in September 2015 and founded by entrepreneurs, OakNorth is a digital bank focused on the lower mid-market (businesses with £$1m-$100m in turnover), that are seeking to scale but may not be served by traditional banks. To date, OakNorth has provided over $24bn in lending to thousands of entrepreneur-led businesses across the UK and US, supporting the creation of more than 70,000 jobs.  OakNorth is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority and the Prudential Regulation Authority.

About Community Unity Bank

Launched in 2022, Community Unity Bank is a FDIC-insured community bank in Oakland County, Michigan. The bank offers a full suite of banking products and services and was formed by bringing together entrepreneurs from around Oakland County with diverse backgrounds to meet a growing need for small business lending.
